title: Variance-scaled coordinate influence bound
statement: Let $n\ge2$ and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ take values only in $\{-1,1\}$. Under the uniform measure on the Boolean cube, some coordinate $i$ satisfies $\operatorname{Var}(f)\frac{\log n}{30n}\le\operatorname{Inf}_i(f)$, where variance and coordinate influence are computed under that measure.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the Boolean cube
replaced: Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be a function on the uniform Boolean cube in dimension $n\ge2$. Some coordinate $i$ satisfies $\operatorname{Var}(f)\log n/(30n)\le I_i(f)$. For a real cube function $h$, define $I_i(h)=\tfrac14\mathbb E_x(h(x)-h(x^{(i)}))^2$, where $x^{(i)}$ flips coordinate $i$ and $\mathbb E_x$ is uniform expectation.
